annotation_description: Playing Urza's Tower on turn 1 produces only 1 colorless mana, which isn't enough to cast anything meaningful this turn. Without Urza's Mine or Urza's Power-Plant in hand, the Tron synergy is unlikely to come online. Playing Ancient Tomb instead would produce 2 colorless mana (at the cost of 2 life), enabling casting Grim Monolith on turn 1. With Grim Monolith's 3 mana plus Voltaic Key untap shenanigans, this opens up a much more explosive turn 1 (potentially casting Glaring Fleshraker or setting up for a powerful turn 2). Alternatively, playing Urza's Saga starts its lore counter progression, which is valuable for its chapter abilities. Urza's Tower with no other Tron pieces in hand is the weakest land drop here.

Casting Mox Diamond before playing a land is suboptimal sequencing. The player will need to discard a land to Mox Diamond, and they should play their land drop first to preserve resources. With Dark Depths + Thespian's Stage combo in hand, they want to maximize their land drops. Playing a land first (like Thespian's Stage or Urza's Saga) and then casting Mox Diamond discarding a less important land would be better sequencing. Additionally, with 3 Urza's Sagas, Wasteland, Yavimaya, Dark Depths, and Thespian's Stage in hand, they have plenty of lands but should still play land before casting Mox Diamond to ensure they don't accidentally sequence incorrectly with the discard.

Discarding Yavimaya, Cradle of Growth to Mox Diamond when it could be a valuable land to play. Yavimaya makes all lands Forests, which is largely irrelevant in this colorless deck, but the player has 3 Urza's Sagas and a Dark Depths/Thespian's Stage combo. However, the real issue is that discarding Wasteland would have been slightly better - Wasteland is a one-shot effect land, while Yavimaya at least has niche utility. Actually, looking more carefully: the hand has Dark Depths + Thespian's Stage (the combo), 3 Urza's Sagas, Wasteland, and Yavimaya. The deck appears to be a colorless combo deck. Yavimaya is likely the worst card to discard because it enables the opponent's and your own lands to tap for green (irrelevant for colorless), BUT actually Yavimaya could interfere with Urza's Saga by making it a Forest - though Urza's Saga already has land types so this shouldn't cause issues. The real consideration is that with 3 Urza's Sagas in hand, you have plenty of lands to play, and Wasteland provides disruption against the opponent's Urza's Tower (Tron piece). Discarding a redundant Urza's Saga would preserve Wasteland for disrupting Tron while keeping Yavimaya as a potential land drop. However, Yavimaya in a colorless deck has very little utility, so this discard is arguably fine. On reflection, discarding an Urza's Saga (having 3 is redundant since you can only use one saga chain at a time effectively) to preserve Wasteland for Tron disruption AND Yavimaya as a land drop might have been marginally better, but Yavimaya is close to a blank in this deck.

Playing Urza's Saga delays the Dark Depths + Thespian's Stage combo by at least one turn. Playing a combo piece (Dark Depths or Thespian's Stage) now allows the combo to come online turn 3, while Saga pushes it to turn 4 since Saga will be sacrificed after Chapter III on turn 3, losing the mana source needed to activate Stage.

Cast Glaring Fleshraker before playing Ancient Tomb from hand. Playing Ancient Tomb first would provide additional mana, potentially enabling both Fleshraker AND Kozilek's Command in the same turn (with Voltaic Key untapping Grim Monolith). With Fleshraker already on the battlefield, casting Kozilek's Command would trigger Fleshraker's ability for extra value (Spawn token + ping).

With Dark Depths and Thespian's Stage both in hand, the player should be setting up the Marit Lage combo as quickly as possible. Playing Dark Depths this turn (or Thespian's Stage) would allow the combo to be completed next turn. Instead, playing Wasteland delays the combo by a full turn. While Wasteland could theoretically disrupt the opponent's Tron lands, the opponent already has Glaring Fleshraker on board and is developing quickly. The Depths-Stage combo produces a 20/20 flying indestructible creature which is likely the fastest path to winning. Additionally, the Urza's Saga on board is on chapter I and will advance to chapter II next turn - playing a second Urza's Saga would be redundant and the first Saga can search for an artifact on chapter III. The correct play is Dark Depths now, then Thespian's Stage next turn to immediately copy Dark Depths and create Marit Lage.

Playing Urza's Saga instead of Urza's Tower or Ancient Tomb is suboptimal here. The player already has Urza's Workshop (an Urza's land) and Urza's Tower. Playing a second Urza's Tower would give them two Urza's lands, making Workshop tap for 2 colorless with Metalcraft (they have Voltaic Key and Grim Monolith as artifacts, need one more for Metalcraft). More importantly, Urza's Saga is an Enchantment Land that will be sacrificed after reaching chapter III, making it a temporary resource. The opponent also has a Wasteland that could destroy it. Playing Ancient Tomb would give immediate access to 2 colorless mana (at the cost of 2 life), enabling a larger Kozilek's Command. Playing Urza's Tower would be a permanent land that contributes to the Urza's land synergy with Workshop. The Saga only taps for 1 colorless on chapter I and doesn't advance the Urza's land count for Workshop's Metalcraft ability. Additionally, they already have an opponent with their own Urza's Saga, so the constructs race may not favor them.

Haiku Coach passed priority with unused mana potential and meaningful plays available. They could untap Grim Monolith (using 4 mana from Urza's Workshop with metalcraft if available, or Urza's Tower + other lands) to generate additional mana, then cast Kozilek's Command for value. They also had an Ancient Tomb and Urza's Tower in hand as a land drop. Passing here wastes a turn of development when the opponent has Wasteland threatening their lands and Urza's Saga ticking up. The Grim Monolith untap would provide significant mana advantage, and Kozilek's Command could create tokens that synergize with Glaring Fleshraker for damage and board presence.

Missed casting Kozilek's Command for X=0 using Urza's Workshop (which produces 2 colorless with metalcraft from 3 artifacts and 2 Urza's lands). Player had exactly {C}{C} available from Urza's Workshop and Urza's Saga (chapter I), which is enough to cast Kozilek's Command with X=0. Drawing an extra card is significant value, especially in a game where both players are developing.

annotation_description: The opponent has Urza's Workshop, Urza's Tower, Urza's Saga, Grim Monolith, and Glaring Fleshraker on board - a very threatening position generating massive mana and token value. Wasteland should be used to destroy a key land (likely Urza's Workshop to cut off metalcraft mana production, or Urza's Saga to prevent the chapter III artifact tutor). Instead, the player spent 2 mana and tapped their Urza's Saga to make a Construct token, which is much lower impact. The Construct would be a 0/0 that gets +1/+1 per artifact (only Mox Diamond = 1/1), making it very small. Meanwhile, the opponent's board is snowballing with Glaring Fleshraker triggers and Urza's lands. Destroying Urza's Saga before it reaches chapter III (to fetch an artifact) or destroying Urza's Workshop (to limit mana) would have been much more impactful. Additionally, the player has Dark Depths + Thespian's Stage combo in hand and should be focused on assembling that rather than making a tiny Construct.

With Exploration on the stack (about to resolve), Gem3F Libby will be able to play an additional land each turn. The combo requires both Dark Depths and Thespian's Stage on the battlefield, plus 2 mana to activate Stage's copy ability. Playing Dark Depths first is fine since Exploration will let them play Stage next. However, the opponent has Urza's Saga which will search for an artifact (potentially Pithing Needle or similar answers) and has a developing board with Glaring Fleshraker. The real question is whether playing Thespian's Stage first would be better to have the colorless mana available, but Dark Depths doesn't tap for mana anyway. The sequencing seems acceptable - they'll play Dark Depths now, then after Exploration resolves they can play Stage as their additional land drop this turn. Actually, wait - Exploration is on the stack, meaning it hasn't resolved yet. They're playing Dark Depths as their normal land drop. Once Exploration resolves, they can play Stage as their additional land. This sequencing is correct for executing the combo this turn. But there's a critical issue: they need 2 mana to activate Thespian's Stage. They have Mox Diamond (untapped) for 1 mana, and their other lands are tapped (Wasteland) or don't produce enough. Yavimaya makes all lands Forests, so Dark Depths would tap for G. Stage would tap for G too but needs to tap as part of its own ability. So they'd have Mox Diamond (1) + Dark Depths/Forest (1) = 2 mana, enough to activate Stage targeting Dark Depths for the combo! This is actually the correct play - they're setting up the Marit Lage combo this turn.
